publicReleaseNotes: Lanyard 0.1.5 moves the RER CLI pin from 0.2.98 to 0.2.144, lets a business run Lanyard with outbound email off, and adopts Base's current agent door. MAIL_PROVIDER=none needs no sender or key: email sign-in refuses as mail_unavailable, staff invitations are refused before they are recorded, nothing is sent, and the owner signs in with rer signin. Setup offers "Turn off outbound email". deploy.json now binds MAIL_PROVIDER, MAIL_FROM, MAIL_RELAY_URL and MAIL_ACCOUNT_ID as optional public settings (before, a hosted deploy never passed them to the Worker, so hosted email never sent), and MAIL_API_KEY is optional. The agent door admits no Business token before a signed policy binds the Business, reads the durable Business stop positively, and refuses a detached Business's tokens, held calls and relay pulls. One migration: 0037_agent_door_relay_privacy.sql.
agentUpdateInstructions: Back up first (rer export, or the authenticated transfer client for a hosted copy). Update to v0.1.5, install the frozen dependencies with RER CLI 0.2.144, then rer setup locally or rer deploy --environment <name> hosted: migration 0037_agent_door_relay_privacy.sql removes only provably cross-Business relay memberships and recreates the two relay audit triggers. An installation that sends mail sets MAIL_PROVIDER, MAIL_FROM and MAIL_API_KEY (and MAIL_RELAY_URL or MAIL_ACCOUNT_ID for rer or cloudflare) in the deploy environment or --env-file: 0.1.4 never bound MAIL_PROVIDER or MAIL_FROM on a hosted Worker; MAIL_PROVIDER=none turns mail off and the owner then signs in with rer signin. A paired Business needs its signed policy before Business tokens are admitted.
